operationContexts.label: Prepare 0.05 M Co(AOT)₂ solution
operationContexts.scene_scope_note: Room-temperature/N₂-glovebox/deoxygenated-solvent context applies to the growth protocol; do not imply a numeric temperature or upstream Co(AOT)₂ synthesis.

operationContexts.label: Add water and equilibrate
operationContexts.scene_scope_note: Show the source-defined H₂O/AOT ratio of 2 and vigorous shaking for a few minutes; exact duration/rate and vessel geometry are unreported.

operationContexts.label: Add 1 M aqueous NaBH₄ under vigorous shaking
operationContexts.scene_scope_note: Show aqueous addition and purple-to-black change as reported; do not depict growth inside intact reverse micelles because the source says the large aqueous addition destroys them.

operationContexts.label: Nucleation and growth of Co nanocrystals
operationContexts.scene_scope_note: Room temperature in an N₂ glovebox; numerical temperature, pressure and duration are unreported. Do not depict a heat bath or continuous N₂ flow.

operationContexts.label: Add dodecanoic acid after synthesis
operationContexts.scene_scope_note: Show post-growth ligand treatment/extraction separately from reduction. Acid amount/contact time and completeness of AOT displacement are unreported.

operationContexts.label: Wash with ethanol several times
operationContexts.scene_scope_note: The source says several times; do not replace this with a numeric count or add unreported centrifugation conditions.

operationContexts.label: Disperse washed nanocrystals in hexane
operationContexts.scene_scope_note: Hexane is source-named; exact isomer, volume and redispersion time are unreported.

operationContexts.label: Centrifuge; collect upper hexane phase
operationContexts.scene_scope_note: For S1–S6, distinguish the collected upper hexane phase from the precipitate; speed and duration are unreported.

general_background.title: Formation from dissolved precursors
general_background.summary: When dissolved species become supersaturated with respect to a solid, nucleation and growth can compete with continued precursor conversion. Mixing, complexation and solution chemistry can change that balance.
general_background.label: General background, not the authors' interpretation

reference.title: Mechanisms of Nucleation and Growth of Nanoparticles in Solution

general_background.title: From a metal precursor to reactive species
general_background.summary: A metal precursor supplies the metal, while its ligands and conversion chemistry influence how reactive species become available. Stronger or more persistent coordination can slow release of reactive metal species, while ligand exchange can open alternative conversion pathways.
general_background.label: General background, not the authors' interpretation

reference.title: Mechanisms of Nucleation and Growth of Nanoparticles in Solution

general_background.title: Electron transfer from a reductant
general_background.summary: A reducing agent can supply electrons that change the oxidation state of a precursor. Coordination and competing reactions affect how that electron transfer contributes to particle formation.
general_background.label: General background, not the authors' interpretation
